newsitem.title: USA: Troy, Mich., voters reject $80 mln go referendum.
newsitem.headline: Troy, Mich., voters reject $80 mln go referendum.

text.p: Voters in Troy, Mich., on Monday voted nearly 3 to 1 against a proposal to issue $80 million of general obligation bonds for street projects, the city clerk said Tuesday.

The referendum, rejected with 1,960 votes for and 5,440 votes against, asked residents to approve issuing the debt for up to 20 years for street and street-related improvements in the Oakland County municipality.
A local canvass board certified the results Monday night for the local election, which also included city council seats and advisory referendums, city Clerk Tamara Renshaw said.
About 13.4 percent of all registered voters participated in the election, she said.
